bug_semantics: A ROLE_USER can create a tag whose name begins with a spreadsheet formula trigger such as '=' and attach it to a timesheet. XLSX export joins tag names into an unsanitized string and passes that string to a spreadsheet cell factory/value binder that infers formulas, so an administrator opening the export evaluates attacker-controlled formula content.
flaw_origin: PR #860 member 9a85b737b35f456a6309889ff9759c58de032972 first added tag names to spreadsheet rows with implode(',', $timesheet->getTagsAsArray()) and an inferred-type PhpSpreadsheet setter, without DDE/formula neutralization. Its one-parent tree lacked all tag-export lines. The later OpenSpout rewrite in squash 136104d4b0c75102f3843725ce2a9bdb902dccd9 preserved the flaw by joining tags in ArrayFormatter and passing all values to Cell::fromValue; it is a refactor/carrier, not the original BIC.
ai_marker: absent: git show -s on BIC 9a85b737b35f456a6309889ff9759c58de032972 shows author and committer Kevin Papst <kpapst@gmx.net>, message 'export tags in spreadsheets', and no trailers, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker
evidence: CVE.org record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-42267 is PUBLISHED and describes ROLE_USER tag formula injection affecting >=2.27.0,<2.54.0, patched in 2.54.0; GitHub advisory https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-3XC2-H5R3-WV3R is reviewed and not withdrawn.

git show 9a85b737b35f456a6309889ff9759c58de032972 adds src/Export/Renderer/AbstractSpreadsheetRenderer.php's row cell as implode(',', $timesheet->getTagsAsArray()) through setCellValueByColumnAndRow, while the BIC-tree Tag entity permits '=' because its name has only NotBlank and Length constraints.

git show 136104d4b0c75102f3843725ce2a9bdb902dccd9 shows the 2.27-era OpenSpout refactor creating ArrayFormatter with return implode(', ', $value) and SpoutSpreadsheet with Cell::fromValue($column); its parent c7f0508707661de82f020a31f2eabf92d6ada71c lacks those new paths, but older unsanitized tag export already existed.

At 2.53.0, config/packages/kimai.yaml grants create_tag to ROLE_USER; src/Entity/Tag.php rejects comma only and permits formula prefixes; src/API/TagController.php POST /tags authorizes create_tag, closing the attacker-controlled source to the export sink.

PR #5899 member 240f0514f3df65c830ef824d8b72301fe8f7e668 changes src/Export/Package/SpoutSpreadsheet.php so every non-total string uses new StringCell($column, $style) instead of Cell::fromValue, directly preventing formula inference; squash landing 16703081cdbdf6740dc688b87e62c8130f614e83 carries the fix.

git merge-base --is-ancestor verifies BIC squash carrier ce6ad0bbb8b91b56a03ebc0ba2104c21aad3f656 is in tags 2.27.0 and 2.53.0; fix landing 16703081cdbdf6740dc688b87e62c8130f614e83 is absent from 2.53.0 and present in 2.54.0 (tag commits 999d820d4ca1fb3bb83395ad9bfc73d73b5eb04a and d456cd3ce2ec5d2599d6cce9490f01f67332d77f respectively).
reasoning: The advisory is a live, reviewed vulnerability, not a withdrawn or rejected report. The source is a low-privileged tag name that can begin with '='; the sink is inferred-type XLSX cell creation. History search shows that the OpenSpout code named in the advisory was not the first causal writer: it preserved an already-vulnerable tag export. Decomposing the earlier #860 squash yields its sole atomic member 9a85b737b35f456a6309889ff9759c58de032972, whose tree exactly equals the landed squash and whose immediate parent has no tag-export cell. The vulnerable carrier precedes the advisory's affected 2.27.0 boundary. PR #5899's member 240f0514f3df65c830ef824d8b72301fe8f7e668 directly replaces inferred string cells with StringCell; landing 16703081cdbdf6740dc688b87e62c8130f614e83 is excluded from 2.53.0 and included in patched 2.54.0. The atomic BIC commit object has human author/committer identity and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
